recipes.title: Dulce De Leche

instructions.tip: Using a heavy-bottomed pot will help distribute heat evenly and prevent scorching.
instructions.title: Combine Ingredients
instructions.instruction: In a large, heavy-bottomed saucepan (at least 4-quart capacity), combine the whole milk and granulated sugar. Stir well to dissolve the sugar.

instructions.tip: Watch the mixture carefully as it heats to prevent boil-overs.
instructions.title: Heat Milk Mixture
instructions.instruction: Place the saucepan over medium heat. Stir occasionally until the mixture comes to a gentle simmer. Do not let it boil vigorously.

instructions.tip: Baking soda helps to prevent curdling and promotes even caramelization.
instructions.title: Add Vanilla and Baking Soda
instructions.instruction: Once simmering, stir in the vanilla extract and baking soda. The baking soda will cause a slight foam; stir until it subsides.

instructions.tip: Frequent stirring is crucial to prevent the bottom from scorching and to ensure uniform caramelization.
instructions.title: Simmer and Reduce
instructions.instruction: Reduce the heat to low, so the mixture is just barely simmering. Cook, uncovered, stirring frequently (every 5-10 minutes), for approximately 2 to 3 hours.

instructions.tip: The dulce de leche will continue to thicken as it cools, so remove it from the heat when it's slightly thinner than you want the final product to be.
instructions.title: Monitor Color and Thickness
instructions.instruction: As the dulce de leche cooks, it will gradually thicken and turn a golden amber color. Continue simmering until it reaches your desired consistency and a rich caramel hue.

instructions.tip: You can also tilt the pot; the mixture should coat the back of a spoon and leave a trail.
instructions.title: Test Consistency
instructions.instruction: To test for doneness, drop a small amount onto a chilled plate. If it holds its shape and doesn't spread too quickly, it's ready.

instructions.tip: This initial cooling prevents thermal shock if you plan to transfer it to a container.
instructions.title: Cool Down
instructions.instruction: Remove the saucepan from the heat. Allow the dulce de leche to cool in the saucepan for about 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally.

instructions.tip: Ensure the container is clean and dry to prevent spoilage.
instructions.title: Transfer and Store
instructions.instruction: Carefully pour the warm dulce de leche into a heatproof jar or container. Let it cool completely at room temperature before covering and refrigerating.

nutrition.calories: Approximately 120-150 per 2 tablespoon serving (estimates may vary based on final reduction)

tips: Always use a large, heavy-bottomed pot to prevent scorching and boil-overs.
Stir frequently to ensure even cooking and to prevent the bottom from sticking.
Be patient! Dulce de leche requires low and slow cooking for the best results.
The color will deepen as it cools.

alternatives: 2% Milk (will result in a less rich dulce de leche)
Half-and-half (will be richer and cook faster)
Brown Sugar (will add a slightly deeper, molasses-like flavor)
